html:
The settling of Cyrene in eastern Libya, about 631 BCE, by Greeks from the island of Thera (Santorini). It grew into the leading Greek city of Africa.

Herodotus tells the story. After years of drought, the people of Thera asked the oracle at Delphi what to do, and were told to found a city in Libya. A small party led by Battus tried an island off the coast, then a site on the mainland, and finally, guided by local Libyans, settled on a high plateau near a spring. Battus's family ruled as kings for some 200 years.

Cyrene was part of the wider Greek colonisation of the Mediterranean, and its farmland, horses and the medicinal plant silphium made it rich. Its founding brought eastern Libya into the Greek world for a thousand years. For the city itself see Cyrene.
